turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The strongest training examples are in the special high-strength heat-treatment regime with `NT=930`, `CT=930`, substantial `Ct`, `DT≈850–896`, low final tempering (`TT=160–200`), and alloying with Ni/Cr/Mo. These samples reach about 1000–1144 MPa, well above the high-Si 845/430–500 group (~700–906 MPa) and all conventional quenched/tempered groups.

I therefore prioritized pool candidates that lie in this 930/CT930 regime and are closest to the top training analogs. The best analog is candidate `c081`, which matches the composition/process family of the training maximum target 1144 MPa except for the final tempering temperature. Candidates `c053`, `c016`, `c062`, and `c063` also sit in the same high-strength cluster or are close variants of training samples around 1030–1110 MPa.

Final: c081, c053, c016, c062, c063
